entries.grounds: The mutant (review_verify.py:167) drops `sort_keys=True` from `_canon`'s json.dumps; the result differs only for a dict whose insertion order is not ascending. None reaches it. The five call sites hand `_canon` ascending order by construction: (1) _stimulus L172 passes the items of plain(frozen stimulus) with a filter that keeps order; BehaviorContract.__post_init__ replaces stimulus and observable by freeze() (contract.py:144), which rebuilds every mapping at every depth as MappingProxyType({k: ... for k in sorted(value)}) (contract.py:37) after requiring str keys (:35-36), and plain() (:53-54) keeps iteration order; (2) L229, (3) L238, (4) L250, (5) L251 pass dicts built `for k in keys` with keys = sorted(...) (L222) as the top level and frozen / plain()'d values below it. json.dumps's sort order is the same code-point order as freeze's sorted() and keys are unique, so sort_keys=True is a no-op on every reachable argument. Every contract reaching anchor() is built by BehaviorContract.create (reproducer_contract L118) or BehaviorContract.from_json (bundle.py:171), both of which run __post_init__. Re-measured at the snapshot: 4,000 random frozen observables with adversarial keys ('', 'é', 'e\u0301', a non-BMP key, '10' vs '9', 'Z' vs 'a', nested to depth 5, lists of dicts): sort_keys True/False dumps equal for every top-level-sorted argument. entries.grounds: What still holds: ensure_ascii only re-spells non-ASCII text, and JSON escaping is a bijection on text without a lone surrogate, so every comparison is unchanged: _stimulus equality (L227) and cardinality (L244), the `outcomes` set (L238), `constant != expected` (L249) - status and contracts were identical in all 1,500 differential cases. A lone surrogate cannot reach _canon: reproducer_contract refuses a surrogate in stimulus/observable/locator (tests/v2/test_v21_defects_reproducer.py:192-205 ReproducerIsNotProse) and an approved contract's hash is over UTF-8. What no longer holds: 'no reader depends on the unescaped text'. The spelling feeds the reason (L229, L250, L251), and the reason feeds detail()'s anchor_why, which round 3 bounds on the ENCODING at WHY_MAX=160 (L269, _fit L332-341, L381): a non-ASCII character of the approved outcome costs 1 body character in the original and `\uXXXX` costs 6 under the mutant (7 once _dumps escapes the backslash, L329). The ids of the approved contracts stand AFTER the outcome in the ANCHORED reason (L251) and the statement carries `anchor` and `anchor_why`, never `contracts` (L379-381), so that tail is the only place the developer's retry prompt names the contracts the block rests on. Measured at the snapshot (two approved contracts BC-V22-S-9-d / BC-V22-S-9-e on two stimuli, a finding stating their common outcome {'stdout': TEXT}, detail() with an Artifact): TEXT = 'Lỗi: không đọc được tệp sổ cái' (30 characters, 10 non-ASCII) -> original: anchor_why ends '(BC-V22-S-9-d, BC-V22-S-9-e)', no `elided`; mutant: anchor_why ends '(BC-V22-S-9-d, BC-V2', elided.anchor_why = 8, the second contract's id cut. With 'ệ' * n the ids are whole up to n=83 in the original and first cut at n=12 under the mutant. In the 1,500-project run 4 of the 98 cases whose reason differs lost an id from the statement. At b5c2457 this window did not exist: the outcome was capped by canon[:200] and the statement by reason[:300], so the ids (about 30 characters) always fitted under either spelling; round 3's 160-on-the-encoding bound created it, and this mutant widens it from 'outcome over 83 body characters' to 'more than 11 non-ASCII characters' (a 30-character Vietnamese message with 10 accented characters is enough; one of 35 characters with 8 loses only the paren).
